comparison: Both evaluations support the theoretical framework (C4, C5, C26-C30). OpenEval emphasizes mathematical grounding and simulation validation (C74), while peer reviewers describe it as 'solid,' 'clever and well-done,' and 'rigorous.' Both agree the framework is well-founded. Peer R1 also includes C6, C8, C37-C38 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Both evaluations support the statistical power analysis (C39-C41, C64). OpenEval provides detailed validation through simulation showing proper calibration and power characteristics. Peer reviewers affirm 'reasonable statistical power in the UK Biobank' and find the method 'promising.' Complete agreement on power analysis validity.

Significant disagreement on UK Biobank results (C43-C50). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to inability to distinguish genetic from environmental causes and lack of external validation for most traits. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the results as credible demonstrations despite acknowledging the same limitations. Peer reviewers view the application more favorably.

Both evaluations address environmental confounding limitations (C52-C55) and rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the lack of direct demonstration of robustness claims. Peer reviewers explicitly identify this as unresolved, stating rejection of null 'does not necessarily point to the favored hypothesis.' Strong agreement on this limitation.

Disagreement on modeling assumptions (C56-C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the impact of violations is not quantified for specific traits analyzed. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting assumptions as reasonable without specific critique. OpenEval is more critical of unvalidated assumptions.

Both evaluations support the methodological innovation and broad applicability (C7, C8, C59). OpenEval emphasizes validation through simulation and UK Biobank application. Peer reviewers call it 'valuable' and affirm it 'will be of interest to researchers,' noting applicability without genotyping. Complete agreement on novelty and utility.

Both address simulation validation (C74). OpenEval includes this in theoretical framework support, showing theoretical distributions match simulated data. Peer reviewers note the method 'rests on a rigorous derivation' and accept validation results. Also addresses C77 (robustness) which OpenEval evaluates separately as uncertain.

Disagreement on future applications (C51, C62-C63, C67-C72). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative possibilities requiring additional development and validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the method as 'promising' with future utility. Peer reviewers are more optimistic about proposed extensions.

OpenEval evaluates historical context and novelty claims (C1, C9-C11, C25) as SUPPORTED, noting well-documented prior work and reasonable characterization of the literature gap. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates biological and evolutionary context claims (C2-C3, C16-C21, C60-C61) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and established knowledge in evolutionary genetics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates standard approaches and prior empirical findings (C12-C15, C22-C24) as SUPPORTED, noting well-supported citations and accurate characterization of the field. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature review claims.
